subject: sociology

moments.title: The Structure of Social Action
moments.body: Parsons synthesises Durkheim, Weber, Pareto and Marshall into a 'voluntaristic theory of action', introducing them to anglophone sociology.
moments.takeaway: A grand synthesis introduces a generation to its predecessors.

moments.title: The Social System
moments.body: Parsons develops a systems-theoretic account of social order, with pattern variables and functional prerequisites.
moments.takeaway: Functional theory aimed at full generality.

moments.title: Family, Socialization and Interaction Process
moments.body: Parsons and Bales analyse the nuclear family in terms of instrumental and expressive roles.
moments.takeaway: Functionalist family theory carried strong gendered assumptions.

now.title: After Parsons
now.body: Parsonsian functionalism declined under conflict-theory and interpretive critique. Neofunctionalists (Alexander) have partially rehabilitated his thinking.
now.open_questions: What does systems theory contribute to climate and ecological sociology?

reflection: Parsons dominated American sociology in the 1950s as much as anyone has dominated a discipline.
